_comment: Spelling rules waiting for adoption. Empty now: P-001..P-011 were adopted by the creator on 2026-11-13 (see adopted_by_creator, and standard.json). New asks are listed here until adopted. NOT applied while here.

not_one_to_one.note: Words the owner corrected differently in each sentence. No single replacement fits, so these are corrected sentence by sentence.

words.corrections: 21 (sam: hair, sentence rewritten) and 22 (a person's name, changed to a Zomi name)
37 (Noteng/Note) and 38 (hih buainate or hih ninte, by meaning)

accepted_in_owner_corrections.note: Words the owner kept in the corrected sentences. They are not in the Tedim Bibles or the dictionary, but they are not errors: they are borrowed words.

words.owner_words: minit is minute, and you can write in English as well
Me or me is vote, and ballot also called me, but it is a borrowed word from Burmese, we can use vote or ballot in Zomi as well
words.note: In correction 34 the owner wrote khutme (a different word, for 'finger' in the English) where the machine wrote khut-me.

words.decision: kept by the owner (2026-11-14: 'thuthang is news, keep it')

words.meaning: we (before the verb); the owner kept it in corrections 71 to 76 and wrote 'eite khempeuh' for 'we all' once
words.decision: treated as accepted (owner said yes, 2026-11-14); not a rule; pairs with `ih` but no 'we' in the English need a sentence-by-sentence look

adopted_by_creator.note: Adopted as rules ZS-001..ZS-011 in standard.json by the creator alone. Full proposal records kept here for traceability.

records.owner_words: I want to use as the Bible uh hi
records.reason: The project owner chose the Bibles' spelling, two words, because 'uh' marks the plural and 'hi' is the verb (owner_example). This also follows the Standard Form tie-break (common published usage first).

evidence.corpus: uhi: 32,520 words in 31,247 pairs; uhhi: 473 words in 464 pairs (language database v2, 2026-11-13)
evidence.tedim_bibles: 'uh hi' as two words 21,496 times; 'uhi' and 'uhhi' 0 times (TDB and TB77)
evidence.dictionary: 'uhi' and 'uhhi' 0 times in the 50K Translation Master
evidence.context: In the corpus 'uhi' appears mostly in pairs about 'they', 'their', 'people', 'each', 'both' (plural subjects), the same use as 'uh hi'
evidence.related: rule check uh-hi lists 'uh hi' and 'uhhi' (the Zolai Standard Format writes uhhi); 'uh hiam' / 'uhhiam' is the same question for the question form and is not part of this proposal
evidence.corpus_two_word_form: 'uh hi' as two words is already the main spelling in the corpus: 142,392 times, against 32,520 for 'uhi' and 473 for 'uhhi'

records.owner_reason: uh is plural and hi is verb, for example: they will go. Amaute pai ding uh hi.

reviews.note: A human review of this spelling decision by a Zomi speaker. The roster code is added when the roster exists. One reviewer is not enough: a second, different reviewer must confirm before the rule is adopted.

records.owner_words: if you see "thil", replace with "na", etc
records.reason: The project owner asked for 'thil' to be written 'na'.

evidence.corpus: thil: 14,379 words in 14,140 pairs (language database v2, 2026-11-13)
evidence.tedim_bibles: 'thil' 0 times; 'na' 9,314 times (it also means other things, see caution)
evidence.other_chin_bibles: 'thil' appears in the Falam Bible (1,620) and the Hakha Bible (2,230), so it may be a word of another Chin language
evidence.context: In the corpus 'thil' appears mostly in pairs about 'things', 'something', 'everything', 'happen'
evidence.tedim_bible_for_things: Aligned with the English Bible, the Tedim word most tied to 'thing(s)' is 'nate' ('na' with the plural 'te'): 112 of 1,504 verses, 6.9 times the usual rate
evidence.caution: 'na' is also a very common word with other meanings in the Tedim Bibles, so the sentences need a Zomi reviewer's check in context. A reviewer may prefer mode 'flag' first, which lists each match and changes nothing.
